### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `78ec0e13f9bb361f34e5f2287c7fb0d72b7cb812` — the merge of head `fd249aeaa97945d033cd776ca49d4611734a9871` into base `53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 78ec0e13f9bb361f34e5f2287c7fb0d72b7cb812 && git checkout 78ec0e13f9bb361f34e5f2287c7fb0d72b7cb812
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 fd249aeaa97945d033cd776ca49d4611734a9871 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350 && git merge --no-ff fd249aeaa97945d033cd776ca49d4611734a9871

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53e3638ea21de79576ff093f9ef476d696941350` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `62f6c360ff8ebd8f295d886c3d668cf113434dc0`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #23514's body and all nine comments (6172542441, 6174591274, 6187670810, 6188859508, 6188959051, 6191875410, 6195283743, 6195318252, 6197627715); PR #23704's body, its three files, and the net diff `origin/main...62f6c360f` (merge base `3bc407d30`, +509/−5). In `protocol.ts` at head I read the cited code: the three callers of `classifyObjectContribution`, `packagelessAddress`, the address block and the D9.9 block of `saveMetaItem`, and its publish-only write-through. I also read the REST save route. The 39 check-runs on the head, at the time of reading: 31 success, 6 skipped by path filter, 2 in progress (Test Core 2/6 and 3/6), 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Check Changeset and Governed Surface Queue Guard are all success. Governing text: ADR-0029 D3 and D9.9; ADR-0070 TL;DR 1, D1 and D5; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3; `clause2-line.mjs`; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (launch-window grade, level axis); `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` signal (4); the seat ruling 6188959051 (refuse with a real way out; option B not taken).

### ① Derived judgments

1. RIGHT: the card's door. A publish save of an object whose registry owner is the `sys_metadata` sentinel, naming package Q, used to answer 200 and store a Q row that nothing served. It now answers 422 `OBJECT_OVERLAY_PACKAGE_MISMATCH` before any write. The diff drops one conjunct (`runtimeOwnerPackageId !== 'sys_metadata'`) and adds an early return for the sentinel only, so the real-package arm's code, status and text are byte-unchanged. It is pinned on a real kernel across a boot: code, status, packageId, ownerPackageId and the first sentence; no row and no history entry stored; owner, data plane and metadata read agree. The ablation went 5 red with the CONTROL green, and the dev walked it over HTTP on SQLite across two restarts. This holds ADR-0029 D3 and ADR-0070 TL;DR 1.
2. RIGHT: the way out, for an object saved in process and for one hydrated at boot (fallback metadata and MetadataPlugin). The two calls are a delete without dropStorage, then the save naming Q. After the delete the object is gone at once (owner, getObject, getMetaItem, data plane 404) and the table keeps its records. Q then becomes the owner and the served definition with the records kept, a boot agrees, and nothing is dropped. This is the dispatch's precondition (re-measure R4 on #23659's heal), and it is met.
3. RIGHT: #23630 member 2. Saves naming P and then Q are both refused, so the rows `[P, Q, package-less]` cannot be produced, across a boot. Pinned.
4. RIGHT: the error code is reused. Its ledger meaning ("a row bound to a package that does not own the object") holds, since no package owns the object. There is no `packages/spec` edit. `ownerPackageId: null` is an in-process property that the REST envelope does not map, and no exported type changes.
5. RIGHT: `applyObjectRegistryMutation` (the rollback and publish-promotion write-through). For a sentinel owner the throw moves from the registry's ownership conflict to D9.9's. Both land in the same best-effort warn, so nothing registers either way; only the warn text changes.
6. WRONG: an unnamed narrowing, and a changeset sentence that is false. The case is legacy residue `[package-less, Q]`: the shape this card's defect wrote (R1, R2), still producible by the promote doors until PR #23683. For it, `packagelessAddress` addresses a save naming NO package to Q's row, because one binding is present and the unbound row is no candidate. So the D9.9 call refuses that save 422 with "Move object 'NAME' into package 'Q' first", although the caller named no package. On `main` it answered 200 and the registry discarded it.
   - The changeset's Unchanged bullet ("A save naming no package over the package-less owner") is false for this population, and no pin covers it: the CONTROL seeds `[null]` only.
   - The prescription misdescribes its own first call here. A DELETE with no package parameter resolves through the same `packagelessAddress` to Q's row, not to "its package-less definition" (R6; kept "by design" in 6188959051).
   - Followed literally, it converges and nothing is dropped. But the 422 and the CHANGELOG describe a different act from the one that happens.
7. WRONG: the remedy text is false for a door this change reaches, the draft door. The D9.9 call is not mode-gated, and the REST route forwards `mode` and `package`, so `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/NAME?package=Q&mode=draft` (Studio's designer door) is refused too. The refusal itself is right, because a Q draft could never go live. But the changeset's Remedy ("send the same PUT again: Q's row becomes the owner at once") is false for a draft. The write-through runs only for `mode === 'publish'`, so after the prescribed DELETE the object answers OBJECT_NOT_FOUND to the data plane until that draft is published. The seat's premise was measured for publish only, and no pin or walk covers the draft door.
8. RIGHT in verdict, with an unnamed change of reason: boot hydration of residue. When the package-less row hydrates first, Q's row is still counted in `loadMetaFromDb` `errors` (D9.9's boot half). Its reason is now this card's prescription, misdirected exactly as in 6. "A boot judges them as before" holds for the verdict only.

### ② Semver level

- RIGHT: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, with the BREAKING banner, the `!` summary and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in the changeset. A narrowing is BREAKING, and it ships `minor` in the launch window. The objectql file is a test, and objectql publishes `dist` only, so no second entry is owed. FROM → TO and the one-line remedy are present, but judgments 6 and 7 make two of its sentences false.
- RIGHT: ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. No stored row, key or export moves, and the remedy is a sequence of requests. The gate printed `[BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required`.
- `Clause-②:` the value `no` is right, since nothing widens. The PR body names no arm, while the changeset carries `(narrowing)`. The body is the one carrier Check Changeset's level axis reads, so the axis read `not-declared` and stood down instead of reading `clean`. AGENTS.md has the changeset carry the PR's own line, so the two should match. Owed: the body line becomes `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The grade is not wrong.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round 1's `needs_decision` (A or B) was answered by 6188959051: A in sequence, B not taken. Its conditions are met: #23659 is on `main`, and R4 is re-measured (two pins and the HTTP walk). Closed.
- Round 1 out-of-scope findings:
  - F1 became #23645 (landed as #23659). Closed.
  - F2 became #23646 (PR #23688, on `main`). Closed.
  - F3 ("a package-less row is not addressable by name beside a package's row", noted by design) is no longer inert. It is the mechanism behind judgments 6 and 8. Escalated into this verdict's rework, not a new card.
- Round 2's open_questions:
  - Q1 (reuse D9.9's code): answered right, see ①.4.
  - Q2 (do not name adopt-orphans in the refusal): answered right. The delete-then-save pair is the narrowest way out, and adopt-orphans rebinds every package-less row of the environment.
- Round 2's deviations:
  - Trailers, the resume push used as the probe, and the void first ablation attempt: accepted.
  - The worktree was cut by detaching the shared checkout's HEAD. That is process, not contract; the seat confirms the shared checkout's state.
  - The Clause-② split between body and changeset: take the edit (②).
- Out-of-scope notes:
  - PR #23683 inherits the sentinel mismatch and this prescription. Whichever PR lands second merges `main` and re-runs the other's D9.9 pins. Right; it should inherit the corrected text.
  - The `applyObjectRegistryMutation` warn is now unreachable from the save door for a sentinel owner. Right.
- Independence, recorded and not a gate: `eca860d38` (the refusal) was written by round 1's mode:subagent run inside session_01GP3comALHRcRBixS2TEnLF, the session this review runs in. Round 2 resumed it.

Owed for a PASS. It is narrow, and the card's door does not change:
1. Changeset: name the residue arm, FROM 200-discarded TO 422 for a save naming no package over `[package-less, Q]`. Its first DELETE removes Q's never-served row. Correct the Unchanged bullet. Name the draft arm, and say the object is unserved from the delete until the draft is published.
2. The refusal message for these two shapes: say what actually happens, or carve the residue case so the prescription stays true. Keep the prescription first, within the 500-character bound.
3. Pins: the residue save naming no package (refused, code and status; the prescribed walk converges with nothing dropped), and the draft save naming Q (refused, code and status).
4. PR body: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, and "a boot judges them as before" names the changed reason.
